title: AlphaProof Nexus Autonomously Proves Quantum-Optics No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional GHZ States
aiSystem: AlphaProof Nexus (Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures + Lean 4)
whyItMatters: AlphaProof Nexus autonomously discovered and Lean-verified a tensor-algebraic no-go theorem settling Krenn’s 2017 photonic GHZ conjecture for all D ≥ N, yielding a new physical optical law.
summary: Posted to arXiv on November 19, 2026 (arXiv:2611.26300) by Mario Krenn, Moritz Firsching, George Tsoukalas, Rishikesh Gajjala, Xuemei Gu, and Swarat Chaudhuri (Google DeepMind, Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, and UT Austin), this work closes a nine-year loop directly descended from Krenn’s 2016 Melvin AI experiments. In 2017, Krenn and coauthors conjectured from AI-designed photonic graphs that linear-optical pair-source networks cannot generate N-photon, D-dimensional Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) states beyond small known cases. Deployed on DeepMind’s Formal Conjectures repository, AlphaProof Nexus autonomously discovered a formal Lean 4 proof establishing that no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for any even N ≥ 4 whenever D ≥ N—constructing a vertex-factored linear functional whose row–column imbalance vanishes on every graph amplitude yet stays nonzero on the GHZ state. The authors then translated the AI’s formal proof into a new physical coincidence principle forbidding such photonic setups.
technicalHighlights: AlphaProof Nexus autonomously discovered a complete, machine-checked Lean 4 proof resolving Krenn et al.’s 2017 photonic GHZ conjecture for all even N ≥ 4 and D ≥ N.
Invented a clean vertex-factored linear functional argument reducing perfect-matching graph amplitudes to an (N−1) × N effective weight matrix imbalance.
Exemplifies true AI-to-human scientific understanding: physicists translated the AI’s formal proof into an interpretable optical coincidence no-go law.
caveats: Resolves the major regime D ≥ N of Krenn’s 2017 conjecture; smaller-dimension cases (3 ≤ D < N) remain open.
institutions: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light

scoreRationale.foundational: Proves a fundamental no-go theorem in high-dimensional photonic quantum entanglement and extracts a new physical law from an AI-discovered proof.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates an end-to-end paradigm where formal AI theorem provers discover new theoretical-physics theorems that humans subsequently interpret physically.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-checked directly in Lean 4 by AlphaProof Nexus and independently read, digested, and physically interpreted by leading quantum-optics authors.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomously cracked a 9-year-old quantum-optics conjecture formalized in DeepMind’s Formal Conjectures benchmark.
